2836.note: The album is the Masonic Stammbuch of Johann Georg Kronauer (Vienna 1783-91, the album with Mozart's entry of 30 Mar 1787 on fol. 41r) and is fully digitised. Fol. 28r carries a whole entry of about twelve lines in an invented alphabet, with a ciphered signature and place/date line; fol. 24r has five short lines of Masonic pigpen beside a drawing, and fol. 31r a pigpen name in an otherwise clear entry of 25 Sep 1784. No decipherment is written on the pages, and none was found in print.

2517.note: Mignet, Négociations relatives à la succession d'Espagne II (archive.org ngociationsrel01mignuoft, pp. 284-285) identifies the volume as AAE Correspondance politique Brandebourg vol. V and uses Millet's letter to Lionne of 24 Aug 1667 for news that is not in the clear part Simson printed (the Brandenburg court told Millet that the margrave of Baden had been refused and was leaving without troops). So the cipher part of the 24 Aug despatch was readable to Mignet from the AAE volume, i.e. a decipherment of it exists there or was made; Simson's 'Vgl. Mignet II p. 285' points to exactly that. For the 27 July despatch ('grösstentheils undechiffrirt') Mignet cites only the despatches of 10 and 20 July, so its state is not established. Not open as a pair; if split, 27 July 1667 needs a look at CP Brandebourg 5.

2938.note: Theal (Records of the Cape Colony III p. 387-388) prints Yonge to Dundas, secret, 6 Jan 1801, sending Prediger's papers 'of which Some Is in Cypher, as the one Part throws Light on the rest', with an abstract; Theal's bracket: 'The Enclosures, excepting a long letter in cypher, are not now to be found.' So the cipher letter survived in the Cape despatches at the PRO when Theal copied them, while Yonge's abstract did not; no decipherment is printed or reported (Dundas, p. 482-483, says only that after Prediger died on passage nothing in the papers implicated his companions). Low confidence because the CO 48 volume is not identified and a London decipherment of 1801 cannot be excluded. Prediger was the Raad der Aziatische Bezittingen's emissary, and the repo's batavia1800 key (Smissaert to C. J. Prediger, 20 Nov 1800) is the first key to try.
2938.access_note: TNA CO 48 (Cape of Good Hope original correspondence), 1801 volume with Yonge's secret despatch of 6 Jan 1801; not described at item level on Discovery (API searches for Prediger, Yonge/Dundas 1801 and CO 48 1801 on 16 Nov 2026 found nothing) and not digitised.
